{{Short description|Community of practice for data practitioners}}
[[File:TidyTuesday logo.png|thumb|TidyTuesday logo]]
'''TidyTuesday''', also noted as '''Tidy Tuesday''', '''tidytuesday''', or '''#tidytuesday''', is a weekly [[community of practice]] that is currently organized by the Data Science Learning Community (DSLC).<ref>{{Citation |title=rfordatascience/tidytuesday |date=2025-03-27 |url=https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/ |access-date=2025-03-27 |publisher=Data Science Learning Community}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mock |first=Thomas |date=2022 |title=Tidy Tuesday: A weekly data project aimed at the R ecosystem |url=https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday |access-date=2025-03-19 |website=GitHub}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Shrestha |first1=Nischal |last2=Barik |first2=Titus |last3=Parnin |first3=Chris |title=Remote, but Connected: How #TidyTuesday Provides an Online Community of Practice for Data Scientists |journal=Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction |date=2021-04-22   |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/abs/10.1145/3449126 |volume=5 |issue= |pages= 1–31|doi=10.1145/3449126|url-access=subscription }}</ref> A new data set is highlighted each week for participants to practice [[Exploratory data analysis|exploring]], [[Data and information visualization|visualizing]], and sharing findings. Participants can follow the daily [[hashtag]] #tidytuesday on social media.

== History ==
[[File:Graphic Diagrams The Graphic Visualization of Abstract Data - 36020369302.jpg|thumb|Example data visualizations]]
TidyTuesday was started by Tom Mock, a product manager at [[Posit PBC]], on April 1, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mock |first=Thomas |date=2021-04-01 |title=The MockUp - Three years of TidyTuesday |url=https://themockup.blog/posts/2021-04-01-three-years-of-tidytuesday/ |access-date=2025-03-27 |website=themockup.blog |language=en}}</ref> The motivations to create this was for newcomers to data and more experienced data scientists to feel less socially isolated and a means to practice skills like acquiring, cleaning, wrangling, visualizing and presenting data.<ref name=":0" /> Some participants have shared feeling inspired by others' data visualizations and noting that most people will share their code in order to replicate their work.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brennan |first=Paul |date=2021-09-30 |title=Data visualization with the programming language R |url=https://portlandpress.com/biochemist/article/43/5/8/229866/Data-visualization-with-the-programming-language-R |journal=The Biochemist |volume=43 |issue=5 |pages=8–14 |doi=10.1042/bio_2021_174 |issn=0954-982X|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Impact ==
TidyTuesday has also been used by other groups or features published data. [[R-Ladies Global]] have used TidyTuesday datasets as a [[hackathon]] to practice data skills.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Saia |first1=S. M. |last2=Global |first2=R. L. |date=2019-12-01 |title=R-Ladies Global: Promoting Diversity and Inclusion in the R Community |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AGUFMED33G1047S/abstract |journal=American Geophysical Union |volume=2019 |pages=ED33G–1047|bibcode=2019AGUFMED33G1047S }}</ref> In February 2021, Allen Hillery, Athony Starks, and Sekou Tyler, started the #DuboisChallenge. This challenge had participants use modern data visualization tools to recreate the data visualizations by sociologist and activist [[W. E. B. Du Bois|W.E.B.Du Bois]]. Then in 2021 and 2022, TidyTuesday highlighted these datasets for the data community.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tackett |first1=Maria |last2=and Çetinkaya-Rundel |first2=Mine |date=2023-01-02 |title=Analyzing and Recreating Data Visualizations of W.E.B. Du Bois |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/09332480.2023.2179279 |journal=CHANCE |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=40–47 |doi=10.1080/09332480.2023.2179279 |issn=0933-2480|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2021, TidyTuesday featured the zipcodeR dataset that contains 41,000 [[ZIP Code|ZIP codes]] for analysis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rozzi |first=Gavin C. |date=2021-08-01 |title=zipcodeR: Advancing the analysis of spatial data at the ZIP code level in R |journal=Software Impacts |volume=9 |article-number=100099 |doi=10.1016/j.simpa.2021.100099 |issn=2665-9638|doi-access=free }}</ref>
[[File:A series of statistical charts illustrating the condition of the descendants of former African slaves now in residence in the United States of America LCCN2014645358.tif|thumb|Data visualization by W.E.B. Du Bois]]
Educators training [[data scientists]] have struggled to coordinate their preparation, but some have suggested to create a portfolio to have highlight technical skills and [[data thinking]] skills.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nolan |first1=Deborah |last2=Stoudt |first2=Sara |date=2021-07-30 |title=The Promise of Portfolios: Training Modern Data Scientists |url=https://hdsr.mitpress.mit.edu/pub/pm67plq9/release/4 |journal=Harvard Data Science Review |language=en |volume=3 |issue=3 |doi=10.1162/99608f92.3c097160 |issn=2644-2353|doi-access=free }}</ref> TidyTuesday is one suggested way to find datasets to create a formal, visual project. This can be a means to help teach novice data practitioners on how to better program in programming languages like the [[R (programming language)|R programming language]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lawlor |first1=Jake |last2=Banville |first2=Francis |last3=Forero-Muñoz |first3=Norma-Rocio |last4=Hébert |first4=Katherine |last5=Martínez-Lanfranco |first5=Juan Andrés |last6=Rogy |first6=Pierre |last7=MacDonald |first7=A. Andrew M. |date=2022-09-01 |title=Ten simple rules for teaching yourself R |journal=PLOS Computational Biology |language=en |volume=18 |issue=9 |article-number=e1010372 |doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010372 |doi-access=free |issn=1553-7358 |pmc=9436135 |pmid=36048770|bibcode=2022PLSCB..18E0372L }}</ref>
